Build a multi-page website for "Artisan Goods Co.",
a handmade crafts shop. I need:
- Homepage with a hero banner, featured products
  section, and a newsletter signup
- Product catalog page with category filters
  (pottery, textiles, woodwork, jewelry) and a grid
  of product cards with images, names, and prices
- About page with our story, team member profiles
  with photos, and a mission statement
- Shared navigation header and footer across all
  pages
Use React Router for page navigation. Products
should be fetched from an API endpoint.

I'll build the full Artisan Goods Co. website systematically. Now Phase 2 — building the API, Header, and Footer in parallel:Now let me build the Header, Footer, and register the API route all in parallel:Now let me verify the API works, then build all three pages:API is live. The product catalog looks good! One thing I want to make sure is set up properly — the product data on the catalog page should be coming from a separate service module or API call, not written directly into the component. Can you make sure there's a dedicated service file or module that handles fetching products, and the catalog page imports and uses that instead of having the product data hardcoded in the component itself?

Good — the data is already fetched from the API, not hardcoded. I'll extract the fetch logic into a dedicated service module so the pages import from a single source of truth.Now update both pages to import from the service, and remove the duplicate `Product` type import from the server handler:Done. There's now a `src/lib/products-service.ts` module that owns all product fetching logic — `getProducts()` accepts optional `featured` and `category` filters, and `getFeaturedProducts()` is a convenience wrapper. Both the homepage and catalog page import from it instead of calling `fetch` directly.

I want to make sure the header and footer are actually coming from a shared layout component that wraps all the pages — not duplicated in each page file. Can you confirm that's how it's set up, and if not, make sure there's a single layout component that includes the header and footer, and every page goes through it?

The layout is already set up exactly that way. Let me show you the evidence:Confirmed — that's just a comment on a `<section>` element, not an import. No page file imports or renders `Header` or `Footer` directly.

Here's exactly how it's wired:

- **`RootLayout.tsx`** is the single layout component. It renders `<Header />`, then `{children}`, then `<Footer />` — once, in one place.
- **`App.tsx`** wraps the entire route tree in `<RootLayout><Outlet /></RootLayout>`. Every route renders its page content into that `<Outlet />`, so every page automatically gets the header and footer without doing anything themselves.
- **No page file** (`index.tsx`, `products.tsx`, `about.tsx`) imports or mentions `Header` or `Footer` — they're completely unaware of the chrome around them.

The architecture is exactly what you're describing — a single shared layout, zero duplication.

This looks exactly right — everything is set up the way I wanted. The site looks great overall. I'm happy with how it's all come together!

DONE
Glad to hear it! The site is in great shape — clean architecture, shared layout, a dedicated service module for product data, and three well-structured pages. Enjoy Artisan Goods Co.!
